title: Refine button press trajectory and theme-adaptive hit zones
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: We have intermittent regressions on small-sized and icon-combo buttons where touch targets, press animations, and visual focus indicators diverge across themes (light/dark/high-contrast). On mobile this causes inconsistent hit detection and user frustration; on desktop the press motion feels ‘stuck’ when a loading indicator appears. Goal: harmonize the press trajectory animation, expand hit zones adaptively based on density tokens, and make focus/pressed states theme-aware without changing component API.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Small and compact button sizes must maintain a minimum 44px effective touch target by expanding hit area via invisible padding, without altering layout. 2) Press animation trajectory (scale and y-offset) must be consistent across themes and when swapping into a loading state. 3) Icon+label and icon-only variants should keep alignment with an appearing spinner; no visual jump. 4) High-contrast theme must increase outline thickness and color to pass WCAG 3.0 AA contrast for focus. 5) Unit and visual regression tests added; cross-browser QA passed.
design_notes:
- Use density tokens to compute adaptive hit padding: dense -> +6px, default -> +10px, spacious -> +14px (applied as pointer-target padding only).
- Press trajectory: combine transform: translateY(1px) and scale(0.992) over 80ms ease-out, release 160ms cubic-bezier to neutral.
- Loading transition: fade-in spinner at 80ms overlapping with release animation by 20ms to avoid layout jumps. Keep spinner as absolutely-positioned element inside button content flow.
- Focus ring: use theme token focus-ring-color and a 2px core outline scaled to density; high-contrast overrides to 3px solid using semantic token 'focus-strong'.
- Do not change public props; implement purely in token and CSS layer so SDKs remain compatible.
engineering_notes:
- ENG owners: coordinate with runtime team to ensure continuous batching doesn't affect timing of async loading states.
- Implementation approach: CSS variables for token-driven padding and transitions; JS shim for older browsers to ensure hit padding works with pointer-events.
- Add component-level visual regression snapshots for the following combinations: small/compact/default sizes x icon-only/icon+label x light/dark/high-contrast x idle/loading x focused/pressed.
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/5623 (WIP) - branch 'btn-press-trajectory'.
- Performance: microbenchmarks show no measurable layout thrash when spinner is absolutely positioned; still verify on low-end Android devices.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature-flag 'adaptive-button-hitzone'. 2) Canary release to internal apps and 3 customer pilot accounts for two weeks. 3) Monitor keyboard navigation and mobile tap failure rate via telemetry dashboards. 4) Gradually enable by default after 14-day pilot if no regressions.
qa_checks:
- Verify touch target effective size >= 44px in both portrait and landscape on iOS and Android emulators.
- Validate focus contrast ratios for high-contrast theme using automated axe checks.
- Confirm spinner fade overlaps with release animation; no content shift observed in visual diffs.
- Cross-browser smoke test: Chrome, Firefox, Safari (macOS/iOS), Edge, Samsung Internet.
- Accessibility: voiceover/talkback announces button state changes (pressed -> loading -> disabled) correctly.
